notes: data/lawsuits.json is kept current by the weekly automated run (scripts/update_tracker.py), which only searches a ~7-10 day window each time. Because the repo launched empty, that narrow window meant the first scheduled run could only find lawsuits filed in roughly the prior week (Jimison) and structurally could not backfill older cases. This 2026-08-04 batch is a manual backfill research pass covering several notable Flock-related suits, added with verified:false pending human review. Aggregate 'as of' figures from external trackers should be checked against, not summed with, this list.

lawsuits.allegation_summary: Filed by ACLU-WV, the Haslam Law Firm, and Glazer, Saad, Anderson immediately after Huntington City Council approved a $2.1 million Flock Safety ALPR contract in a contentious 6-4 vote; alleges the city failed to follow required procedures in awarding the contract, including improper authorization for a private company to use public property for the cameras.
lawsuits.status_detail: Lawsuit filed July 14, 2026, same day as the council vote; ACLU-WV legal director indicated additional legal claims could follow beyond the procedural challenge.

lawsuits.allegation_summary: Aurora police used a Flock-style ALPR hot-list alert that misread a stolen motorcycle plate as matching Gilliam and her family's SUV; officers held Gilliam and four children, including minors, at gunpoint and handcuffed them face-down on pavement during a botched stolen-vehicle stop.
lawsuits.status_detail: City of Aurora settled with Gilliam for $1.9 million (settlement reported 2024, following a 2021 filing over a 2020 incident). Court/case number not confirmed from the sourcing reviewed for this entry. Most contemporaneous 2020-2021 coverage described the system only as a license-plate-reader hot-list match without naming the vendor; later retrospective reporting on Flock misuse (e.g. CNN, 2026) cites this case as a Flock example -- flagged for maintainer verification of the ALPR vendor.

lawsuits.case_name: Upchurch v. City of Toledo, et al.
lawsuits.court: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Ohio
lawsuits.allegation_summary: A Flock camera misread the "7" on Upchurch's license plate as a "2", falsely matching it to a stolen-vehicle hot list; Toledo police stopped Upchurch, and an officer released a police K9 that bit and injured him even though the truck was correctly his own, non-stolen vehicle.
lawsuits.status_detail: Federal case Upchurch v. City of Toledo, et al., No. 3:25-cv-00711 (N.D. Ohio). Reported settlement of $35,000 with the city and an officer (2025).

lawsuits.court: First Judicial District Court, Rio Arriba County, NM (case number not confirmed)
plaintiffs: Unnamed minor sister (12, identified in reporting by initials D.D.)
lawsuits.allegation_summary: A Flock Safety camera misread the plaintiffs' license plate (ending in 2, misread as 7) as matching a stolen vehicle; Española police stopped, handcuffed, and detained Gonzales and her 12-year-old sister at gunpoint before discovering the error.
lawsuits.status_detail: Filed January 3 (year approximate, ~2024) in New Mexico state district court. Resolution not confirmed from the sourcing reviewed.

lawsuits.allegation_summary: A Flock camera misread the letter "H" on Burkleo's license plate as "M" (a dirt-obscured character), falsely flagging his car as matching a wanted vehicle; Atherton police stopped Burkleo at gunpoint and ordered him to the ground before discovering the error.
lawsuits.status_detail: Settled with the town and involved officers for $45,000 per news reporting; exact filing date, court, and case number not confirmed from sourcing reviewed. Atherton Police Department publicly denied wrongdoing.

lawsuits.court: U.S. District Court for the District of New Mexico
lawsuits.allegation_summary: Then-17-year-old honor-roll student Adam Pacheco was pulled over and handcuffed at gunpoint by a New Mexico State Police officer based on inaccurate information tied to a Flock Safety camera alert while driving home from Pojoaque High School.
lawsuits.status_detail: Federal case Pacheco v. City of Española, No. 1:23-cv-00593 (D.N.M.). Reporting indicates New Mexico State Police paid $200,000 in connection with the case; city-side resolution not separately confirmed from sourcing reviewed.

lawsuits.case_name: Moore v. City and County of San Francisco
lawsuits.court: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California
defendants: City and County of San Francisco
lawsuits.allegation_summary: Proposed class action alleging that San Francisco police's network of roughly 500 Flock Safety ALPR cameras constitutes "warrantless and unreasonable" mass surveillance in violation of the Fourth Amendment.
lawsuits.status_detail: Filed as a proposed class action against the City and County of San Francisco and SFPD in N.D. Cal.; exact filing date and case number not confirmed from sourcing reviewed. NOTE FOR MAINTAINER: this is the closest verified match found for a suit naming the City/County of San Francisco itself -- I could not confirm a case captioned "Green v. City and County of San Francisco" as requested; please check the exact caption against the source article, or supply a link if you have one, before treating this as the correct entry.

lawsuits.case_name: Hofer v. County of Contra Costa, et al.
lawsuits.court: Likely U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California (venue not confirmed from sourcing reviewed)
defendants: Three Contra Costa County Sheriff's deputies (named individually; names not confirmed from sourcing reviewed)
lawsuits.allegation_summary: An automated license plate reader flagged Hofer's rental car as stolen based on a "stale" database entry -- the vehicle had already been recovered and returned to circulation -- and Contra Costa County Sheriff's deputies conducted a high-risk "felony stop" at gunpoint on Hofer and his brother without verifying the alert.
lawsuits.status_detail: Federal civil-rights suit filed December 2018 against three Contra Costa County Sheriff's deputies (individual civil rights, warrantless search, and excessive force claims) over a November 25, 2018 stop. Contra Costa County settled for $49,500 (paid to Hofer in an August payout). ALPR vendor not confirmed as Flock Safety in sourcing reviewed -- Flock was newly founded in 2017 and this stop predates its market dominance; flagged for maintainer verification before treating as a confirmed Flock case.

lawsuits.court: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California
plaintiffs: Javorsky (lead plaintiff; additional plaintiffs not fully confirmed from sourcing)
lawsuits.allegation_summary: Federal suit against Flock Safety alleging its ALPR network enables unauthorized mass collection and sharing of license-plate data, framed around privacy and data-broker-style claims; part of a wave of 2026 California suits over Flock sharing plate data with out-of-state and federal agencies.
lawsuits.status_detail: At a Sept. 24, 2026 hearing in the consolidated In re Flock Group Inc. ALPR Litigation, Judge Vince Chhabria signaled plaintiffs likely lack Article III standing under California's ALPR law to proceed in federal court and indicated the case would likely be remanded to state court; a case management conference was set for Oct. 9, 2026 with no written ruling confirmed yet.

lawsuits.allegation_summary: Wichita resident and privacy activist Mason Grimmett alleges the city's roughly 200 Flock Safety ALPR cameras, capturing about 900,000 vehicle photos monthly, constitute a warrantless dragnet surveillance program that violates the privacy protections of Section 15 of the Kansas Constitution Bill of Rights. The suit seeks a declaration that the program is unconstitutional and an order requiring removal of the cameras.
lawsuits.status_detail: Petition filed July 30, 2026 in Sedgwick County District Court by the Kansas Justice Institute; cites Wichita's own data showing 904,603 license plate searches in a single month (June 26-July 27, 2026) and prior officer misuse cases (e.g., former Kechi Police lieutenant convicted of using Flock data to stalk his estranged wife).

lawsuits.allegation_summary: Plaintiff alleges she was wrongfully identified via a Flock ALPR camera image (which reportedly captured drivers/passengers, not just plates) and was subsequently falsely arrested and prosecuted by Cumberland, RI police following a traffic stop and car chase involving a different vehicle.
lawsuits.status_detail: Filed in U.S. District Court in June 2026; case surfaced publicly and drew ACLU of Rhode Island pressure on the town council to cancel its Flock contract starting the week of Aug 7, 2026. No ruling reported yet.

lawsuits.court: Michigan state court (county circuit court, exact court not specified in sources)
lawsuits.allegation_summary: Genesee County resident Tewolde, represented by the Mackinac Center Legal Foundation, sued the county after it denied a FOIA request seeking records about its 30 Flock ALPR cameras, including the Flock contract and search logs, with the county claiming a private vendor (Flock) owns the data despite the contract stating otherwise.
lawsuits.status_detail: Lawsuit filed this week (reported ~Aug 20-21, 2026); seeks court order compelling county to turn over requested records.

lawsuits.filed_date: unknown (part of series of requests filed 2024-2025)
lawsuits.allegation_summary: Part of a series of Washington Public Records Act suits by resident Jose Rodriguez alleging local governments failed to timely release Flock ALPR camera images/data he requested, which were often deleted under 30-day retention policies before requests could be fulfilled.
lawsuits.status_detail: Confirmed via late-August 2026 news coverage: case involved both Sedro-Woolley and Stanwood, WA. A Skagit County Superior Court judge ruled July 16, 2026 that both cities wrongfully withheld Flock camera footage from a records requester (Jose Rodriguez). Parties settled for $80,000 total, split $40,000/$40,000 between the two cities; Stanwood approved its portion Aug. 13, 2026 and Sedro-Woolley approved its portion around the same week.

lawsuits.allegation_summary: Nationwide proposed class action alleging Flock's 120,000+ camera ALPR network enables 'rampant' misuse by law enforcement for stalking/personal surveillance, produces inaccurate license-plate reads at scale, and that Flock has known of and downplayed such misuse as rare 'bad apple' conduct. Claims include invasion of privacy, negligence, negligent design, failure to warn, and intentional infliction of emotional distress.
lawsuits.status_detail: Flock was served September 1, 2026; the judge extended Flock's deadline to answer or otherwise respond to October 30, 2026.

lawsuits.case_name: SecureNet Solutions Group LLC v. Flock Group Inc.
lawsuits.allegation_summary: Patent-infringement suit alleging Flock's camera systems and software (Falcon LPR cameras, Vehicle Fingerprint, FlockOS Real-Time Crime Center, Enhanced LPR software, Flock Safety Platform, and Raven audio device) infringe seven patents related to multi-sensor surveillance data analysis systems.
lawsuits.status_detail: Complaint filed in U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware seeking damages for alleged patent infringement.

lawsuits.case_name: Negrete-Gonzalez (Ellis Collective) v. Regents of the University of California
defendants: University of California Board of Regents (UC Berkeley)
lawsuits.allegation_summary: Suit alleges UC Berkeley failed to adequately respond to a Feb. 17, 2026 California Public Records Act request seeking details about UC Berkeley's Flock ALPR data-sharing settings, audit logs, and the list of agencies (including reportedly CBP) that received shared plate data.
lawsuits.status_detail: Confirmed filed Aug. 28, 2026 in Alameda County Superior Court; alleges UC Berkeley failed to adequately respond to a Feb. 17, 2026 CPRA request for records on UCPD's Flock ALPR data-sharing practices, including sharing with CBP in possible violation of SB 34.

lawsuits.allegation_summary: Institute for Justice-represented plaintiffs allege Norfolk's 176+ Flock ALPR cameras create a warrantless surveillance dragnet that tracked one plaintiff 526 times and another 849 times in about four months, violating the Fourth Amendment.
lawsuits.status_detail: District court (Judge Mark Davis) ruled for the City of Norfolk in late January/early February 2026, finding no Fourth Amendment violation and dismissing the case days before a scheduled bench trial; plaintiffs appealed to the Fourth Circuit (No. 26-1227). On September 21, 2026, the ACLU, ACLU of Nevada, and the Innocence Project (with EFF) filed an amicus brief in the appeal.

lawsuits.case_name: Umemoto v. Westchester County Police Department
lawsuits.allegation_summary: Proposed class action alleging Westchester County's roughly 575-camera ALPR network amassed about 1.6 billion plate scans without proper legislative authorization and shared the data with more than 50 outside agencies, including ICE, in violation of the New York State Constitution.
lawsuits.status_detail: Filed June 9, 2026 in Westchester County Supreme Court by NYCLU, the Policing Project at NYU Law, the Knight First Amendment Institute, and Freshfields LLP. Seeks a declaration that the program is unconstitutional and an injunction halting operation. Newly identified via Oct. 2026 coverage of related Rockland County Flock opposition; no docket activity reported in the last 7-10 days.

lawsuits.case_name: Elser v. Flock Safety, Inc., et al.
lawsuits.court: U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado
defendants: Columbine Valley Police Chief Bret Cottrell
lawsuits.allegation_summary: Plaintiff alleges a Flock camera search led police to wrongly issue her a criminal summons for a $25 porch theft, which was voided after she proved her innocence; claims include negligence, invasion of privacy, and unlawful search.
lawsuits.status_detail: Filed Oct. 5, 2026 in U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado, Case No. 1:26-cv-04977. Plaintiff Chrisanna Elser alleges Flock camera data was used by a Columbine Valley Police Sgt. to wrongly summon her for a $25 package theft; names Flock Safety, Towns of Columbine Valley and Bow Mar, Police Chief Bret Cottrell, and Sgt. Jamie Milliman; seeks class treatment and punitive damages.

lawsuits.case_name: NoCams Muskego, et al. v. Waukesha County, et al.
lawsuits.court: U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Wisconsin (removed from Waukesha County Circuit Court)
lawsuits.allegation_summary: Suit by Wisconsin Institute for Law & Liberty argues warrantless law-enforcement searches of Flock ALPR databases violate the Fourth Amendment and seeks to require a warrant before database searches.
lawsuits.status_detail: As of Oct. 7, 2026, Waukesha County law enforcement defendants have responded to the lawsuit and the case has moved to federal court per WTMJ reporting.

lawsuits.case_name: Greer v. Flock Group, Inc., et al.
lawsuits.court: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida
lawsuits.allegation_summary: Pro se plaintiff alleges the city's combined network of 126 ALPR/license-plate-reader devices (53 Flock, 73 Axon) constitutes a warrantless search violating the Fourth Amendment.
lawsuits.status_detail: Case No. 2:26-cv-14319-AMC; amended complaint filed August 2026, receiving renewed news coverage Oct. 11-12, 2026.

lawsuits.case_name: Murkerson v. Flock Group Inc., Coweta County, et al.
lawsuits.allegation_summary: Proposed class action alleging Coweta County Sheriff's deputies used Flock's nationwide ALPR network to track plaintiff's vehicle in retaliation for a prior excessive-force lawsuit; alleges Flock failed to require verifiable investigative justification for searches, enabling misuse.
lawsuits.status_detail: Filed Oct. 8, 2026 in U.S. District Court, Newnan Division. Seeks class-action status for Georgia drivers searched without documented investigative justification, plus damages and injunctive relief (record deletion, removal from watch lists).

lawsuits.case_name: ACLU of Wisconsin & EFF (ex rel. Wisconsin Council of Churches) v. City of Green Bay, et al.
lawsuits.allegation_summary: Direct petition to the Wisconsin Supreme Court arguing warrantless police searches of ALPR/Flock databases violate the Wisconsin Constitution's prohibition on unreasonable searches, citing impacts on churchgoers' privacy (e.g., attending AA/NA meetings, domestic violence services).
lawsuits.status_detail: Petition filed directly with Wisconsin Supreme Court Oct. 14, 2026, asking the court to take the case directly rather than proceed through lower courts; court has not yet decided whether to accept the petition.
